children: , the wireless-chip and connectivity company, jumped about 3.1% to $185.82 Tuesday morning even as MediaTek turned up the pressure on its premium Snapdragon franchise. Reuters reported that MediaTek's new Dimensity 9600 Pro uses 2-nanometer manufacturing and delivers a claimed 51% improvement in initial generative-AI prompt processing. The stock's strength suggests investors are looking beyond a fresh competitive threat and focusing on Qualcomm's broader growth story.

Qualcomm generated $9.9 billion of fiscal third-quarter revenue, with handset-chip sales contributing $5.1 billion. Automotive revenue surged 61% to a record $1.6 billion, while combined automotive and internet-of-things revenue increased 28%. That diversification matters because Qualcomm is increasingly trying to make smartphones only one part of the investment case rather than the entire story.

Handsets still represented roughly 51.5% of total quarterly revenue, so MediaTek's latest flagship chip is attacking Qualcomm where the dollars remain biggest. At the same time, the chart shows Qualcomm at $185.815 versus a GF Value of $175.82, leaving the shares 5.68% above GuruFocus' estimate of fair value. Investors are already paying a modest premium for diversification into automotive, AI software and data centers; the next test is whether Qualcomm can defend Snapdragon economics while those newer businesses keep scaling.

title: Qualcomm Jumps Over 3% as MediaTek Fires a 2nm Warning Shot
